newsitem.title: USA: NiGas limits Ill. gas storage withdrawals.
newsitem.headline: NiGas limits Ill. gas storage withdrawals.

text.p: Northern Illinois Gas Co, a unit of NICOR Inc, has declared "critical day" for Saturday natural gas deliveries due to the bitter cold in the Midwest, the company said Friday.

"It's anticipated that this will hold true for Sunday too. We'll re-evaluate it on Monday," a company spokeswoman said, noting storage withdrawals would be limited into NiGas' seven underground facilities.

A critical day, which affects gas deliveries for the day beginning at noon (1200 CST) on Saturday, can be declared from November 1 to April 1 when storage withdrawals and supplies from NiGas based on contracted quantities need to be limited.
The limit is typically caused by severe cold.
Any additional gas used by the customer will be charged at $6.00 per therm plus the cost of the gas, the company said.
NiGas also said that one of its suppliers, Natural Gas Pipeline, which runs from western Texas to Illinois, has also declared a critical day.
NGPL, however, was not immediately available for comment.
Early cash prices for weekend deliveries at the Chicago city-gate were talked around $6.25 per mmBtu.
